extraction.name: SeamlessM4T
extraction.description: SeamlessM4T is a massively multilingual and multimodal machine translation system that supports speech-to-speech translation, speech-to-text translation, text-to-speech translation, text-to-text translation, and automatic speech recognition for up to 100 languages. It is designed to bridge the gap between direct and cascaded models for speech translation in large multilingual and multimodal settings by combining a strong speech representation learning model with a massively multilingual text-to-text translation model. The system is built using 1 million hours of open speech audio data to learn self-supervised speech representations with w2v-BERT 2.0, and a multimodal corpus of automatically aligned speech translations, dubbed SeamlessAlign, totaling 470,000 hours. The system achieves significant improvements over state-of-the-art models in various translation tasks and is evaluated for robustness, added toxicity, and gender bias.

extraction.rai:dataCollection: The data collection process involved gathering 1 million hours of open speech audio data to learn self-supervised speech representations with w2v-BERT 2.0. Subsequently, a multimodal corpus of automatically aligned speech translations, dubbed SeamlessAlign, was created by filtering and combining human-labeled and pseudo-labeled data, totaling 406,000 hours. The process included speech-language identification, gathering raw audio and text data at scale, speech mining, and using a novel multimodal embedding space (SONAR) to project both modalities into a joint embedding space for mining.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Physical data collection, Software Collection, Web Scraping, Experiments
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data collection involved 4 million hours of raw audio originating from a publicly available repository of crawled web data, with approximately 1 million hours in English. Text data was sourced from the NLLB dataset, including data sources, cleaning, and filtering steps run at scale with the Stopes library.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: The data collection process was conducted over an extended period, with the raw audio data sourced from a publicly available repository and text data from the NLLB dataset. The SeamlessAlign corpus was created by filtering and combining human-labeled and pseudo-labeled data, totaling 470,000 hours.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The data manipulation process included deduplication of audio file URLs, resampling at 16KHz, filtering out non-speech data with a bespoke audio event detection (AED) model, and applying an over-segmentation approach to split audio files into shorter chunks. Additional filtering steps included toxicity filtering to remove pairs with toxicity imbalance and length filtering to remove utterances shorter than 0.1 seconds or longer than 50 seconds.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The data preprocessing protocol involved deduplication of audio file URLs, resampling at 16KHz, filtering out non-speech data with a bespoke audio event detection (AED) model, and applying an over-segmentation approach to split audio files into shorter chunks. Text data was cleaned and filtered using the Stopes library. Additional steps included toxicity filtering and length filtering to remove noisy or misaligned pairs.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations were created using a combination of human-labeled data, pseudo-labeling with a multilingual T2TT model (NLLB-200-3.3B), and parallel data mining using the SONAR embedding space to identify translation pairs. The process included filtering based on toxicity imbalance and length to ensure high-quality training data.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: The annotations were created using the Stopes library for text data processing and the SONAR embedding space for speech data mining. Human-labeled data was sourced from open-source datasets, and pseudo-labeling was performed using the NLLB-200-3.3B model.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The annotation analysis involved evaluating the quality of annotations by comparing human-labeled data with pseudo-labeled data and mined data. The process included filtering based on toxicity imbalance and length to ensure high-quality training data. The annotations were used to train the SeamlessM4T models for various translation tasks.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: The number of human labels per dataset item varied depending on the task and data source. Human-labeled data was used for primary training, while pseudo-labeling and parallel data mining were used to augment the dataset. The annotations were filtered and combined to create a high-quality training corpus.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: The machine annotation tools used included w2v-BERT 2.0 for self-supervised speech representation learning, NLLB-200-3.3B for pseudo-labeling, and the SONAR embedding space for parallel data mining. The Stopes library was used for text data processing and filtering.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The data release maintenance plan includes open-sourcing the metadata to recreate the unfiltered 470,000 hours of SeamlessAlign, providing tools for creating aligned speech data, and offering inference code and fine-tuning recipes. The plan also includes providing a text-free S2ST automatic evaluation model (Blaser 2.0) and supporting the community with resources and documentation.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset includes sensitive human attributes such as gender, socio-economic status, geography, language, age, culture, and experience. The data collection process involved gathering speech audio data and text data from various sources, including publicly available repositories and datasets.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset has significant social implications, including augmenting world-readiness by enabling on-demand access to multilingual speech translation. It supports accessibility for individuals with visual impairments and those who rely on speech-based interfaces. The system also addresses the multiscript conundrum for languages with script variance and supports low-resource languages, bridging the translation gap between high and low-resource languages.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset exhibits biases in gender representation, with masculine lexica overrepresented compared to feminine in the analyzed datasets. The system also shows overgeneralization to masculine forms when translating from neutral terms, with an average preference of ~10% towards masculine forms. Additionally, the system shows a lack of robustness when varying gender by ~3%, indicating gender bias in translation outputs.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Known limitations include data generalization limits, quality issues, and non-recommended uses such as long-form translation, domain-specific inputs (e.g., medical or legal domain), and certified translations. The system is not intended for production deployment and may produce toxic, biased, or false outputs. The model's performance may vary based on gender, race, accent, or language, and it may struggle with translating slang or proper nouns across high and low-resource languages.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for training, testing, validation, and fine-tuning of machine translation models. It supports various use cases, including automatic speech recognition, speech-to-speech translation, speech-to-text translation, text-to-speech translation, and text-to-text translation for up to 100 languages. The system is designed for research purposes and is not recommended for production deployment or certified translations.
